title: Move a flap lever through its gated quadrant to full flap
instruction: Put the white flap lever of the grey quadrant trainer in its FULL detent, next to the red end stop, then let go.
context: Aircraft mechanics and service technicians (O*NET 49-3011.00) carry the flap selector along a two-lane gated slot in the flap-system operational check: lift it out of its detent, jog it sideways round the go-around gate wall at 15, which no lift clears, and drop it into the far notch at FULL. This is a gated path, not a single detent change: the lift, the carry to 15 and the sideways jog must come in order at set places, and no other route reaches FULL. The task uses a light desk-top flap-quadrant procedure trainer. A free-standing desk-top trainer has to be steadied while its spring-loaded handle is lifted, and this one weighs less than the knob's lift spring, so one hand holds it down while the other works the lever.
setup: Station table; world metres, x forward from the arm bases (at x 0, y +-0.305), y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. One free-standing flap-quadrant trainer, 0.50 kg in all, lever pivot at world (0.33, -0.12, 0.7875), lever travelling from UP (vertical) toward the robot (world -x) to FULL, pivot axis along world y. (1) Base: grey anodised aluminium sRGB (0.55, 0.57, 0.60), 0.42 kg: a 170 x 230 x 4 mm base plate on rubber feet (friction 1.0/0.9) from world x 0.22 to 0.39 and y -0.19 to +0.04; pivot cheeks and housing side plates; a grey 40 x 10 x 50 mm hold-down handle tab, centre (0.355, -0.02), top z 0.8015. (2) Gate plate (part of the base): dark steel sRGB (0.25, 0.26, 0.28), an arc 20 mm deep (70 to 90 mm from the pivot), 80 mm wide, from 12 deg behind UP to 50 deg; a two-lane slot: the inboard lane (world -y side) runs UP to 15 and ends in the gate wall, the outboard lane (16 mm toward +y) runs 15 to FULL; 6 mm detent teeth leave notches UP, 5, 15, 30 and FULL 10 deg apart (FULL at 40 deg); end stops at both ends, the one just past FULL painted red sRGB (0.80, 0.12, 0.10). (3) Lever: white aluminium shaft sRGB (0.92, 0.92, 0.90), 10 mm diameter, 0.03 kg, on a gimbal (10 g yoke) at the pivot; a sideways spring (0.6 N m/rad) holds it in the inboard lane. (4) Knob: white ABS sRGB (0.95, 0.95, 0.93), 0.04 kg, a 30 x 22 x 30 mm flap-handle block 140 mm from the pivot (world z 0.9275 at UP) on a 12 x 12 mm sleeve that slides 12 mm up the lever against a spring of 60 N/m preloaded to 6 N; under it a steel gate pin, 8 mm diameter and 30 mm long across the slot, rests in the UP notch.
scoring: Measured every control step from reset: lever pitch (deg from UP toward FULL), sideways angle and knob lift (mm) from the trainer's joints; trainer displacement = largest move of 6 points on the base (plate corners, gate plate, handle) from where it was placed; knob speed and spin from its pose change between control steps; each gripper's pad clearance to the trainer and its speed. Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, so setting the trainer back never clears it). Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: the trainer moved more than 10 mm. Seated = lift under 1 mm. Ladder: 0.25 = pin seated past the go-around gate (pitch 25 deg or more: the 30 or FULL notch) at the end; 0.5 = pin seated in the FULL notch (pitch within 1 deg of 40) at the end; 0.75 = 0.5 with the knob still (under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s) for the last 1 s; 1.0 = 0.75 and the release gate: every pad of both grippers at least 30 mm from the trainer and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: the detent marks and the pin in its notch on a top photo; a taped outline and ruler for the 10 mm move; video for stillness and release.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the knob, move the lever back through the jog to the inboard lane and drop it into the UP notch (vertical lever, pin seated). Stand the trainer back on its taped outline at the placed position, handle tab toward the robot's left. Check the knob drops under its spring and the lever springs to the inboard lane on its own.
fidelity: Rigid links and box/cylinder colliders: the gate plate's arc is 5.7 deg chord segments (under 0.2 mm off the arc). The knob spring (6 N preload) and the 0.50 kg trainer are light so the soft simulated arm can lift and hold them; a real trainer is heavier with a stiffer spring. The sideways tilt is a gimbal at the lever pivot. Joint stops stand in for the lift stop and the inboard spring stop. Printed position labels are not modelled; the red end stop marks FULL.
